retained_mechanisms: single-expert tiles of at most BM rows per expert run (partial tiles only at a run's end), expert-major tile order, max_tiles = ceil(M / BM) + min(E, M)
seg (single-buffered BK 64/128) and db (double-buffered BK 64) schedules, tile-on-x (GX 32) or mlx (column, tile) grid, PAD threadgroup bytes
affine dequantization: fp32 scale * q + bias rounded once to bf16
16x32x16 NAX tensor ops in mlx's K order with fp32 accumulation; K tail only in valid 32-deep sub-steps (unused at admitted shapes)

fused [gate; up] table paired by pair_row so each lane holds gate and up of the same output element; both rounded to bf16, then Multiply()(Multiply()(g, Sigmoid()(g)), u) with MLX's functors (the compiled nn.silu(gate) * up op sequence)
row map: sorted row r reads token row rmap[r] in place (32-bit element offsets rmap * K + col), never materialising x[order // k]
32-bit row offsets (no >32768 padding needed; seam padding tolerated as a trailing repeat of the last row)

admission.contract: affine 4-bit group 64, bfloat16 activations/scales/biases, uint32 packed weights, fused [gate; up] table [E, 2I, D/8], down [E, D, I/8], x_tokens [T, 1, D], hidden_sorted [M, 1, I]
admission.row_block: rows = T * k >= 16 and rows // experts >= 4 (overrides oMLX M >= 8)

named_geometries.default35b: E256 k8 D2048 I512: first admitted T = 128
named_geometries.flash_next: E512 k10 D2560 I640: first admitted T = 205

admission.overflow: rows + 63 <= INT32_MAX - 4096 (MAX_ROWS: scan loop g0 += 4 * 1024, shapes, params; entry-time rows incl. seam padding re-checked per projection); D, I <= INT32_MAX // 32 (MAX_DIM = 67108863; largest aligned accepted dim 67108800); per projection rows, K, N (incl. 2I), 4 * max_tiles and every dispatch-grid dimension <= INT32_MAX (grid computed on the host by dispatch_geometry, as oMLX _launch); signed_int_intermediates of the CHOSEN plan (planned or pinned) <= INT32_MAX: K * kBits, N + 63, NAX fragment offsets 24 * ld, seg (bm - 32) * K (unmapped) and (bm - 32) * ld_out, seg 16 * K, db 31 * K + 28 (unmapped); T * D < 2**32 (uint row-map element offsets); pinned gx only the upstream 0 or 32. These are generic host bounds, not a native qualification of general shapes
admission.signed_bounds_note: Root 2940/2942 proposed D, I <= INT32_MAX // 32, which covers K * kBits and the db 31 * K + col. The retained seg schedule also forms x + tm * K (unmapped down) and y + tm * N / tm * ldy with short tm up to bm - 32 = 96, so seg 96/128 plans need the per-plan check: for example, down K = I = 2**25 (below the floor) with 96 rows per expert plans seg 128 and 96 * K = 3,221,225,472 > INT32_MAX; it is refused. The corrected root examples T4/k4/E4/D2**29/I64 (mapped K * 4 = 2**31) and T16/k4/E4/D64/I2**28 (plain down db r * K) are refused. D = 2**28 alone in the mapped gate/up does not reach a plain down K (down K = I): the earlier opus example in radio 2943 was wrong.
admission.values: sorted expert ids in [0, E), each expert ONE contiguous run, row map in [0, T) with every token exactly top_k times, row_map == order // k and inv_order inverse of order when an order is supplied, sorted_experts == expert_ids[order] when router ids are supplied, padding rows repeat the last real row; the research entry requires routes sorted from router ids (expert_ids and order present)
admission.gate_revalidation: sealed objects are not trusted by identity alone: the gate re-runs admit(admission.request) and requires equality, and revalidates routes (bounds, runs, order, row map, router-id binding) and requires equality, so dataclasses.replace() copies that keep the seal cannot pass altered content
refused: routes without router ids/order at the research entry

planner: Port of oMLX _plan at d6b2b92 (thresholds measured upstream on M5 Ultra at Qwen3.8 / GLM-5.3 / MiMo-V2.6 expert shapes). NOT measured or tuned in mlx2; no environment override.
state_boundaries: implemented: research candidate only; qualified false; selected false; observed_used false; route None
decide_route always returns ordinary-reference; supplied evidence (smoke, host report, receipt) never promotes
research_opt_in=True is an acknowledgement that an explicit call may build/dispatch Metal kernels; it is NOT GPU ownership (the caller must hold the GPU lease per lab protocol)
every refusal precedes the first MLX import and any kernel construction; capability and backend errors propagate unchanged; no fallback, no canary, no timers, syncs or readbacks

engagement counters: fixed keys, saturating at 2**63 - 1. {native,substituted}.successful_chains.{gate_up_mapped_swiglu,down_segmented} count lazy dispatch chains whose tile scan AND matmul both returned into the graph; they are not every issued scan (a scan issued before a raising matmul is not counted) and NOT GPU executions. backend_raised counts calls whose backend construction, capability check or dispatch raised (the exception propagates unchanged). The former native.scan/substituted.scan keys are retired. A future engagement gate needs a fresh successful chain AND an evaluated, checked output. No timers, syncs or readbacks.

native classification: native only when the entry constructed the backend itself via _native_backend AND type(backend) is the _MLXBackend class captured at import as a default argument; a supplied instance or subclass, a rebound module name _MLXBackend, or a substituted _native_backend factory (including one returning an _MLXBackend subclass) counts as substituted.
